---
title: "Continuous outcomes: development API and qualification"
output: rmarkdown::html_vignette
vignette: >
  %\VignetteIndexEntry{Continuous outcomes: development API and qualification}
  %\VignetteEngine{knitr::rmarkdown}
  %\VignetteEncoding{UTF-8}
---

The dedicated continuous API models transformed assay values with Gaussian or
Student-t observations. Features share a residual-variance prior, while location
coefficients use fixed priors. It does not impose a sum constraint. Student-t is
the default and its scale is adjusted so the reported residual variance is the
actual observation variance. Features are conditionally independent; residual
cross-feature covariance is not modeled.

This is a development API. Passing one fit's HMC diagnostics does not establish
statistical calibration or publication readiness. The package's validation
campaign must qualify the intended assay, design and decision rule separately.

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(eval = FALSE)
```

Supply complete long data with one finite `value` for every sample-feature pair.
Use independent-unit metadata explicitly; sample covariates must be constant
within a sample. Negative transformed values are allowed. Incomplete assays,
duplicates and rank-deficient designs are rejected.

```{r}
fit <- sccomp_estimate_continuous(
  assay, ~ condition + (1 | donor), ~ 1,
  sample = sample, feature = feature, value = value,
  family = "student_t", cores = 4, chains = 4,
  iter_warmup = 1500, iter_sampling = 1500, mcmc_seed = 10102026,
  adapt_delta = .995, max_treedepth = 12
)
fit
```

Global scaling uses the median of all values and the median positive feature
MAD. It preserves between-feature relative scales. Location effects, residual
variances, random SDs, predictions and residuals return to original input units.
Using `scaling="none"` requires explicitly supplied assay-unit priors. Empirical
scaling conditions inference on a data-derived transformation; exact-model SBC
therefore uses explicit priors without that transformation.

The long result identifies `feature`, `component` and `parameter`, and reports
`estimate`, `lower`, `upper`, `rhat`, `ess_bulk` and `ess_tail`. Global observation
df has `feature=NA`. Sampler CSVs and fit metadata are retained. The fit's
posterior-draw attribute is portable; keep it to predict or test after reloading.

```{r}
tested <- sccomp_test(fit, effect_threshold = 1)
predicted <- sccomp_predict(fit, summary_instead_of_draws = FALSE)
replicated <- sccomp_replicate(fit, number_of_draws = 100)
residuals <- sccomp_calculate_residuals(fit)
```

`effect_threshold` is required and uses original input units. Selection uses
posterior probability that the chosen effect direction exceeds the threshold;
its complement includes both effects within the threshold and the opposite
direction. Cumulative mean error probabilities define `posterior_fdr` within features for
each component and contrast. This is a posterior expected error rule. Its
frequentist operating characteristics require separate simulation evidence.

## Meaningful effects and posterior error

An effect can be precisely estimated while remaining too small to matter.
For a threshold of 1 log2 unit, an effect near 0.2 with a narrow interval is
evidence for a small change, but is not a discovery under this decision rule.
Choose the threshold from the scientific question before inspecting results.

| Quantity | Interpretation |
| --- | --- |
| `p_null` | Posterior probability of an effect within the minimum-effect interval |
| `p_false_sign` | Posterior probability of the opposite sign, including zero |
| `p_error` | Posterior probability that the chosen direction fails to exceed the threshold |
| `posterior_fdr` | Cumulative mean `p_error` in one component/contrast discovery family |

`p_error` includes both the interval null and effects in the opposite direction;
do not add `p_null` and `p_false_sign`, since those events overlap. A posterior
expected error of 5% describes the fitted model's uncertainty. Realized false
discoveries across repeated datasets require an independent calibration study.
Limma `treat()` and dream `getTreat()` also test minimum effects, using a
frequentist decision rule. Compare them with identical data and thresholds.

## Known technical covariates

Fit measured nuisance covariates jointly so their coefficient uncertainty
contributes to the treatment posterior. A batch can affect both the location
and residual variance:

```{r}
fit_batch <- sccomp_estimate_continuous(
  assay, ~ condition + batch + (1 | donor), ~ condition + batch,
  sample = sample, feature = feature, value = value,
  family = "student_t", mcmc_seed = 10102026
)
sccomp_test(fit_batch,
  contrasts = list(location = c(treated_control = "conditiontreated"),
                   log_variance = c(treated_control = "-2 * condition1")),
  effect_threshold = 1, variance_ratio_threshold = 1.5
)
```

This example requires observed batch metadata and an identifiable design. When
batch and treatment coincide, the model cannot separate their effects and
rejects the rank-deficient design. Joint covariates do not propagate uncertainty
from normalization performed before fitting, and do not model unknown latent
factors. The frozen airway example contains no invented batch covariate.

The decision framework follows Lewin, Bottolo and Richardson (2018),
*Bayesian methods for gene expression analysis*, sections 2.3 and 4.1.
Adaptive biological-effect shrinkage is a separate, gated extension; this v1
model retains its fixed biological-effect priors.

Variance covariates use centered sum coding, so their coefficient names and
interpretation differ from location treatment coding. For two levels `control`
and `treated`, a variance coefficient named `condition1` represents half the
control-minus-treated log-variance difference:

```{r}
fit_v <- sccomp_estimate_continuous(
  assay, ~ condition, ~ condition, "sample", "feature", "value"
)
sccomp_test(fit_v,
  contrasts = list(location = c(treated_control = "conditiontreated"),
                   log_variance = c(treated_control = "-2 * condition1")),
  effect_threshold = 1, variance_ratio_threshold = 1.5
)
```

Only linear arithmetic is accepted in contrast expressions. Backtick coefficient
names containing punctuation. Location and log-variance discovery families stay
separate. The HMC selection gate requires four chains, zero divergences and
treedepth saturations, Rhat<1.01, bulk/tail ESS>=400 and chain E-BFMI>0.3.
VI is exploratory; selection additionally requires `allow_exploratory=TRUE` and
the result keeps its exploratory marker. Prior-only fits cannot select effects.

Predictions use the complete fitted specification by default. `formula_location`
can retain a subset of fitted fixed terms and whole random clauses; replication
also accepts `formula_variance` to retain selected variance terms. This filters
the fitted coefficients and preserves their coding; it does not refit or
reparameterize the model. Removed intercepts lose their original-unit centering
offset. All fitted covariates remain required in sample-wise `new_data`.

Sample-wise
`new_data` must use fitted factor levels and observed random-effect groups.
Draw outputs contain `sample`, `feature`, `.draw`, `generated_value`, `location`
and `residual_variance`; summaries average posterior location/variance and
summarize generated observations. Residuals subtract posterior mean location
from observations and standardize by the square root of posterior mean residual
variance. They use every retained draw without generating replicated values.

Continuous outlier-removal refits, proportional fold change, and unwanted-effect
removal are unavailable. Use the Student-t family for robust observation noise.
The optional observed-mean variance trend conditions moderation on observed
feature means; it is not a fully generative Bayesian mean-variance trend.

Few grouping levels weaken random-effect estimation. Within-group slope
variation and a full-rank random/residual covariance basis are required.
Correlated binary intercept/slopes with only two observations per
group cannot separate residual from random-effect covariance and are rejected.
Repeat each condition within groups or simplify the clause. Proper priors do
not resolve missing likelihood information. Interpret random
variance/correlation estimates with the design and sensitivity checks in view.
